Hi Liam —

Great to meet on Friday. Per our call, attaching a concise plan to handle the SDK endpoint migration and expected client-side retry behavior so your engineering team can validate before the cutover. Key items below and attached: integrify-sdk-quickstart.md (SDK snippets + config), cutover-plan-v1.xlsx (schedule + owners).

Summary / asks
- Cutover window: propose Thu 2026-11-26 22:00–23:30 PT (low traffic). Can you confirm the window or suggest an alternative?
- Primary tech contact: please confirm Sara Kelly (sara.kelly@integrify.com) for network/firewall coordination.
- Pre-cutover checklist: we need you to verify TLS, outbound IP allowlist, and rate-limit header handling (see migration checklist).

Technical notes (high level)
- SDK setup: the new endpoint is api.redistribution.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams. The provided quickstart includes an explicit base_url override and migration guide for old endpoints. (See integrify-sdk-quickstart.md)
- Retries & timeouts: recommended client policy: initial timeout 6s, per-request max timeout 30s. Use exponential backoff with full-jitter; max attempts 5 for idempotent calls. For streaming requests, prefer shorter connect timeout (3s) and keep token refresh separate.
- Rate limits: our gateway emits the following headers on 429s: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch sec). We recommend client-side leaky-bucket and local token-bucket with small buffer to avoid spikes.
- Endpoint migration approach: DNS cutover + 30s health-check window; clients should gracefully retry on connection-refused or 502 with backoff. We include sample curl and SDK snippet in the quickstart.

Next steps
- Please confirm Sara and the cutover window by EOD Tue 2026-11-24.
- If okay, we will circulate the final cutover runbook and DocuSign SOW link for signatures.

Attachments: integrify-sdk-quickstart.md, cutover-plan-v1.xlsx

Thanks,

Thanks Tessa — this looks good and thorough. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock the window:

1) Backoff semantics: can you confirm whether retries should treat 502/503 the same as 429? Our infra team prefers distinguishing rate-limit (429) from transient (502/503) so they can apply a slightly higher max attempts for transient errors.
2) Sticky sessions: our customer-facing gateway uses session affinity for streaming. Will switching DNS break existing long-lived streams, or do you recommend letting them drain?

Sara will be our network lead; I looped her in. If you can add a 1-paragraph note about token refresh during long-lived streams (we use short-lived JWTs), that would be helpful.

We can tentatively accept Thu 11/26 22:00 PT pending Sara's check on firewall rules.

Adding the sample curl + small implementation notes below. Will upload migration-checklist.md to the Drive by EOD.

Sample curl for a quick smoke test against the new endpoint (replace API_KEY):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \  
  "https://api.redistribution.redwood-inference.com/v1/health"

Rate-limit behavior: our gateway returns headers; prefer the client read X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset. If Remaining == 0, pause until Reset + 500ms. For 429s, use exponential backoff with full jitter and cap at 60s.

Implementation hint for clients: leaky-bucket on the client with a small local buffer (10–20 tokens) smooths bursts. For streaming clients that use session affinity, signal drain by returning HTTP 408 for new attach attempts during cutover window to avoid breaking in-flight sessions.

Timeline: I will have the checklist and curl tests in Drive by Thu 2026-11-26 14:00 PT.
